update_log: Baseline initialization of high-frequency National and International Days, organized chronologically with historical significance for Static GK.

january_to_april.significance: Marks the return of Mahatma Gandhi from South Africa to Mumbai in 1915.
Celebrated on the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda.
Commemorates Field Marshal K. M. Cariappa taking over as the first Indian Commander-in-Chief in 1949.
Initiated by the Ministry of Women and Child Development to raise awareness about the rights of the girl child.
Marks the foundation day of the Election Commission of India in 1950.
Led by the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) to raise worldwide awareness.
Marks the discovery of the 'Raman Effect' by Indian physicist Sir C.V. Raman (1928).
Global day celebrating the social, economic, cultural, and political achievements of women.
UN observance highlighting the importance of freshwater.
Marks the day in 1882 when Dr. Robert Koch announced his discovery of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
Marks the anniversary of the founding of the World Health Organization (WHO) in 1948.
An annual global event to demonstrate support for environmental protection.
Marks the passing of the Constitution (73rd Amendment) Act, 1992 that institutionalized Panchayati Raj.

may_to_august.significance: Dedicated to workers and laborers globally.
Commemorates the successful Pokhran-II nuclear tests (Operation Shakti) in 1998.
Created by WHO to draw global attention to the tobacco epidemic.
The UN's principal vehicle for encouraging worldwide awareness and action for the environment.
Proposed by India and adopted by the UN; coincides with the Summer Solstice.
Honors the legendary physician and second Chief Minister of West Bengal, Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy.
Seeks to focus attention on the urgency and importance of population issues.
Named after the successful 'Operation Vijay' in 1999 to evict Pakistani intruders from the Kargil sector.

may_to_august.day_name: International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples
may_to_august.significance: Also known as World Tribal Day; promotes and protects the rights of the world's indigenous population.
Birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi; promotes national integration and peace.
Celebrated on the birth anniversary of hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand.

september_to_december.significance: Birth anniversary of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, India's first Vice-President and second President.
Marks the adoption of Hindi written in Devanagari script as the official language of the Republic of India (1949).
Commemorates the date of the signing of the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer in 1987.
UN observance corresponding with Mahatma Gandhi's birthday.
Marks the official foundation of the Indian Air Force in 1932.
Anniversary of the entry into force of the UN Charter in 1945.
Birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the 'Iron Man of India'.
Birth anniversary of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, independent India's first Education Minister.
Marks the adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly in 1949.
Global initiative to unite in the fight against HIV, support people living with HIV, and commemorate those who have died.
Celebrates the achievements and role of the naval force; commemorates Operation Trident during the 1971 Indo-Pak War.
The day the UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in 1948.
Birth anniversary of the legendary Indian mathematician Srinivasa Ramanujan.
Birth anniversary of Chaudhary Charan Singh, the 5th Prime Minister of India, recognizing his championing of farmers' causes.
Observed on the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
